parsed.explanation: The combined regime is hostile at two levels. Nationally, entry screening is a universal-exposure measure: visa officers are instructed to refuse applicants where documents cast 'reasonable doubt' on sex, with suspected misrepresentation carrying a permanent fraud bar, and the passport regime now issues only birth-sex markers, with documented confiscations stranding travelers. State-level, the jurisdiction ranks among the worst for anti-trans legislation: birth-certificate changes are closed (surgical exception), forcing disclosure when documents are examined; state-run facilities may restrict use per birth sex; and a documented arrest — handcuffed, held 24 hours in the men's ward — shows the facility law operating. A trans minor travelling with a parent faces a care ban, school disclosure rules and a climate prosecuting facilitation. Protections are real but partial: national hate-crime statute, employment ruling, courts enjoining several orders. No organised sweeps or lethal pattern; severity sits at arrest, misgendered custody and exclusion, not imprisonment-as-typical.

entry_documents.exposure: Universal-exposure: visa officers must refuse where records cast reasonable doubt on sex; wilful misrepresentation can trigger permanent fraud ineligibility; trans athletes barred; foreign passports scrutinised against appearance; foreign governments issued advisories after detentions of their citizens over visa issues.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four elements, never automatic; limited waivers exist; policy is litigated and some orders enjoined; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at adjudication can escalate to fraud investigation, refused entry, or stranding abroad; a minor's documents face the same screen.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented state arrest for facility use: trespass charge, handcuffing, 24 hours held in the men's ward. National corrections bureau mandates haircut, hormone removal, conversion-style therapy for trans inmates; immigration custody shows forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute; courts have enjoined several orders; detention was brief and bail/release followed.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A bathroom encounter can move from restriction to arrest to misgendered custody; immigration detention applies to any visitor losing status.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State law allows restriction of bathroom use in state-run facilities; criminal trespass in defined circumstances with documented first arrest. National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; many states layer similar bans.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Trespass offence requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, with exemptions (chaperoning, emergencies); most other state bans are civil only; 29+ states and capital district have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The operative rule the traveller meets in state buildings is the state statute; the national order reaches federally funded facilities nationwide.

care_services.exposure: Providing gender-affirming care to minors is illegal in the state; national rules propose barring public insurance reimbursement for under-18 care; hospitals subpoenaed for under-19 patient records nationally.
care_services.protection: Adult visitors' care is not criminalised in this state; conversion therapy banned for licensed counsellors; national employment ruling persists.
care_services.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a guardian faces care denial and record exposure; a parent seeking care for the child touches an enacted felony-level provider ban.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State platform language accusing trans people of preying on women; national 'gender ideology' removals; counterterrorism strategy targeting 'radically pro-transgender' groups; schools directed to investigate and prosecute facilitation of minor social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism text disclaims targeting mere disagreement; courts enjoined several orders; 2022 poll shows 78% statewide support for anti-discrimination law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing raises outing severity by legitimising official suspicion, but documented enforcement against visitors is limited to the facility arrest.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor care ban (2023, veto-proof); schools must disclose trans students to parents and forbid pronoun accommodation requirements with penalty provision; teacher prosecution directive nationally; college/high-school groups may discriminate against LGBT students; sports bans.
minors_guardians.protection: Pronoun-bill overlap and enforcement instances unresolved; no documented enforcement of penalty provision; tribal nations hold two-spirit traditions.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling trans minor cannot safely socially transition in state schools; guardian exposure flows through disclosure and care laws, not through parental liability itself.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated incident of anti-trans violence in the state is documented; hate-crime statute excludes gender identity; police response to trans victims undocumented. National bias statistics are LGB-wide and carry no denominator here.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime prosecution available since 2009; municipal protections in one city; general rule of law functioning; the solitary documented arrest drew civil-rights criticism.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of documented street violence is not evidence of safety in a thin-data axis, but state-level incident record is silent.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: State has no gender-identity anti-discrimination statute or hate-crime coverage; birth-certificate marker closure forces disclosure whenever state documents are shown; tracker marks it a negative-law jurisdiction among the worst states.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Driving licences and state IDs update marker on a physician/therapist letter — a working partial remedy; national courts accept suits and have blocked orders; oversight and litigation are active.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Which documents get believed at entry, and custody placement after any arrest, remain open questions; licence relief does not cure the closed birth certificate.

anchor_checks.comparison: Karthovia features systematic police stops, confiscations and fines with near-universal visitor exposure. This regime is less systematic in daily street policing, but its entry regime carries a severer consequence — permanent fraud ineligibility — and its facility law has produced a criminal arrest with misgendered custody. Net: somewhat above 0.35-B, not far.

Drellia's registration database creates durable universal exposure with harassment and eviction as typical harms, no custody threat. This jurisdiction has comparable universal exposure (document regime, entry screening) plus a documented criminal facility charge and a worst-tier legislative ranking, but also stronger national remedies. Slightly below 0.45-D to comparable.

Valdoria's checkpoints produce questioning and overnight holds without criminal charge, with legal-aid and consular remedies. This regime can refuse entry outright on 'reasonable doubt', bar for life on fraud findings, and has arrested a trans person under its facility law. That severity places it below 0.55-A.

Meridia shows organised extortion of trans travellers at terminals with sealed police logs and ineffective oversight. This jurisdiction lacks a documented extortion pattern, its courts function, and its national hate-crime statute and litigation channels operate. Clearly above 0.25-B.

Meridia's trained border officers, written detention reasons and compensation route mark a protective entry posture. This regime's entry posture is the opposite — officers instructed to refuse on sex doubt — and its state layer adds criminalised facilities. Well below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime a visitor encounters is the national entry/document system fused with a worst-tier state layer. Entry screening is universal exposure: the visa cable's reasonable-doubt refusal instruction and lifetime fraud bar reach every trans applicant whose documents or presentation invite scrutiny, and the passport-marker regime has already stranded travelers. Within the state, birth-certificate closure forces disclosure wherever state documents are checked; state-run facilities may exclude, and the record's one documented enforcement — handcuffed, held in the men's ward — proves the pathway from restriction to criminal custody is live, not hypothetical. A trans minor additionally meets an enacted care ban, mandatory school disclosure and a teacher-prosecution directive, making family travel materially riskier than solo travel. These exposures are not offset by resident-facing machinery and are only partially cushioned by functioning national courts, the 2009 hate-crime statute and enjoined orders. No organised sweeps, extortion pattern or lethal violence is documented, keeping severity at arrest, misgendered custody and exclusion — placing the jurisdiction in the upper Elevated band, well above extortion-tier 0.25 anchors but clearly below remedy-working 0.55–0.65 anchors.
